courses.title: Environmental Engineering Design and Decision Making
courses.description: Environmental Engineering design and decision-making, analysis tools and techniques, data illustration and other communication techniques, professional development including ethics and equity. Subject themes include water, air and soil. [3-0-2]. Prerequisite: Second-year standing in ENVL. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Technical Communications for Environmental Engineering
courses.description: All aspects of technical communication, including report preparation, business correspondence, and oral presentation, applied to environmental engineering specific cases and projects. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of APSC 176, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 112, ENGL 120, ENGL 121, WRDS 150. Corequisite: ENVE 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: One of APSC 176, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 112, ENGL 120, ENGL 121, WRDS 150

courses.title: Environmental Engineering Science
courses.description: Analysis of integrated environmental systems, quantification of fundamental chemical and biological processes, systems design, evaluation of environmental impact, future trends. [3-2-0]. Prerequisite: All of CIVL 204 and CHBE 241, and either CHEM 154 or all of CHEM 121, CHEM 123. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of CIVL 204 and CHBE 241, and either CHEM 154 or all of CHEM 121, CHEM 123

courses.title: Environmental Engineering and Sustainability
courses.description: Sustainability vocabulary and systems theory relevant to environmental engineering practice, foundational sustainability topics including those relating to urban ecology, industrial ecology/circular economy, and humanitarian engineering, stakeholder analysis, communication, and adaptive change leadership skills [3-0-2] Prerequisite: ENVE 200.

courses.title: Environmental Engineering Intermediate Design Project
courses.description: Real-time, fully-integrated, conceptual and detailed design experiences that address an ill-structured, socially and technically complex environmental engineering problem for communities with consideration to the cultural history and needs of the communities. Restricted to students in ENVE or ENVL with third-year or higher standing. [2-0-3] Prerequisite: ENVE 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Environmental Engineering Capstone Project
courses.description: Application of chemical, biological, and environmental science; engineering concepts; sustainable development and health and safety considerations; engineering economics; and life cycle analysis. Conceptual and detailed design for a multi-scale and complex environment health and protection problem. [2-0-4; 2-0-4]. Prerequisite: All of CHBE 244, CHBE 373, ENVE 301 and fourth-year standing in ENVL. Corequisites: CIVL 402, CIVL 416. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of CHBE 244, CHBE 373, ENVE 301 and fourth-year standing in ENVL
